transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Vu (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Galaxy CTO), Ethan Ross (Galaxy Head ML), Lina Gomez (Infra)

Summary: initial cost/unit economics discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private, sample workloads and budget constraints (~$10k/mo to start). Discussed batching, prefix/KV cache, quantization levers, throughput expectations and pilot benchmarks. Agreed next steps to share pricing spreadsheet and benchmark runbook.

Topics: pricing tiers, per-token economics, batching impacts, cache strategy, Dedicated reserved pricing, pilot scope, security (VPC/KMS), SLA expectations

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, quick intros, I'm Jordan Kim, AE at Redwood. Samira's our SE, she'll cover benchmarks.
[00:00:10] Maya: Hi, Maya Chen, CTO at Galaxy Ventures. We fund and operate a couple of AI teams, looking at inference infra economics.
[00:00:15] Ethan: Ethan Ross, head of ML. We're mainly running multi-turn summarization and a reranking pipeline.
[00:00:20] Lina: Lina Gomez, infra, I'll ask about VPC and network stuff.
[00:00:25] Samira: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: we want to understand your workloads, target latency/cost, then show how Redwood levers - batching, caching, dedicated - move the cost per token.
[00:00:35] Maya: Sounds good. Our constraint: budget is conservative to start, roughly $10k/month for inference, but we expect to grow. Right now approx 5M tokens/day peak across batches, 1.2M active users monthly, but that's fuzzy.
[00:00:50] Ethan: Typical requests are mult-turn, average sequence length in prompts ~400 tokens, outputs ~150 tokens. We also do embedding calls for search, maybe 10M vectors/month in index updates.
[00:01:05] Jordan: OK. So that's helpful. On the pricing side we have hosted per-token tiers (we went over a baseline earlier) and then dedicated/reserved where unit cost is lower once you commit capacity. The big levers are: batch size, KV/prefix cache for repeated prefixes, and quantized model variants. But let's talk numbers.
[00:01:25] Samira: To give a ballpark: on hosted with moderate batching, you might see e.g. $X per 1k input+output tokens for the model family we recommend - that varies by model. With Dedicated reserved capacity, your per-token compute costs drop substantially because you're amortizing GPU runtime and can run quantized kernels. For 5M tokens/day, cost differentials can be 30-60% depending on batching and cache hit rate.
[00:01:50] Maya: Sorry can you repeat that number, 30-60%? Against hosted baseline?
[00:01:55] Samira: Yes Vs hosted baseline. So if hosted is say $1.00 per 1k tokens (example baseline), dedicated might effectively be $0.4 - $0.7 per 1k tokens assuming good batching and high cache reuse. (Note: these are demo figures - we'll send a proper spreadsheet).
[00:02:12] Ethan: The key for us is latency. Most of our front-end calls require <=300ms p95. Will batching push us past that?
[00:02:20] Samira: Great question. Batching has knobs: continuous batching and latency SLO. You can configure max-wait or max-batch-size. For your SLOs we typically keep max-wait small (~10-15ms) for interactive traffic, but you still get batching wins because many requests align. For very low-latency tails, we use prioritized lanes or smaller instance pools to serve critical requests.
[00:02:40] Jordan: Also caching is big for you - with mult-turn chat the prefix/KV cache can return a huge percent of keys for repeated sessions or system prompts. If you have similar prompts across users (like a standard system prompt for summarization), cache hit rates can be 40-70% reducing per-token compute.
[00:02:55] Maya: Our prompts have a stable system prefix but user content varies. Is that enough for a good hit rate?
[00:03:01] Samira: Yes, system prefix reuse helps a lot for the first KV steps; for later steps caching less effective unless conversation patterns repeat. For reranking and embedding pipelines, we can do deterministic caching of embeddings and memoization where appropriate.
[00:03:15] Lina: On dedicated vs private: we're in a regulated fund, so VPC and KMS are non-negotiable. Private on-prem is probably overkill but VPC + customer-managed KMS is required. Does that change pricing?
[00:03:25] Jordan: Private and VPC options are supported. VPC/private deployments add a platform fee for the control plane and networking, and Dedicated reserved capacity pricing reflects that. We can build that into TCO - often Dedicated in a VPC ends up between hosted and full private on-prem in terms of unit cost. We'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[00:03:42] Ethan: For embeddings - we do batch index updates overnight, so latency isn't an issue. How do you price embeddings? Per-embedding unit or per-token?
[00:03:49] Samira: Embeddings are typically priced per vector or per-embedding unit; they tend to be cheaper. We'll show a split. For nightly batch indexing you can use cheaper instance types, scheduler jobs on Dedicated, or even private infra to reduce unit price.
[00:04:05] Maya: We want a pilot: run our top-3 workloads (real-time summarization, multi-turn chat, and nightly reranker) with Redwood hosted and a small dedicated pool to compare costs and latency. What does that look like?
[00:04:17] Samira: Typical pilot: 2 weeks, we run 3 workloads with representative traces. We'll collect token counts, p50/p95 latencies, batch sizes, and cache hit rates. We'll provide the runbook and scripts. We need a dataset sample, and an API key for instrumented runs.
[00:04:34] Ethan: How invasive is instrumentation? We don't want to leak PII during tests.
[00:04:38] Jordan: We offer anonymized telemetry collection; you can scrub PII before sending. Also the pilot can run in your VPC if you prefer.
[00:04:45] Lina: What's the expected delta in cost if we enable 4-bit quantized models? We saw quality regressions in earlier experiments.
[00:04:52] Samira: Quantization is a tradeoff. For many reps, we recommend 4-bit or 8-bit with calibration; cost savings are meaningful (20-40% lower compute), but quality impact depends on model and prompt. Part of the pilot is running evals to quantify regen or hallucination rate with candidate quant settings.
[00:05:10] Maya: Can you send a simple TCO example for our numbers? 5M tokens/day, avg 550 tokens per session, 30% cache hit, target p95 < 300ms, budget $10k/mo starting.
[00:05:20] Jordan: Yes - we'll model hosted vs dedicated reserved (1 GPU equivalent) vs dedicated committed cluster and show per-1k token price, monthly spend and tail latencies. We'll include sensitivity to cache hit and batch sizes.
[00:05:34] Samira: For the benchmark config we'll ask for traces and a small synthetic load generator or replay script. We'll provide expected metrics: tokens/sec, GPU utilization, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:05:50] Ethan: What about failure modes - throttling when we hit burst traffic?
[00:05:53] Jordan: Redwood has burst capacity options and routing policies. On Hosted we have quota/burst limits; on Dedicated you can configure burst pools. We also have fallback model variants if a higher capacity model is unavailable - that keeps requests running but possibly at lower quality.
[00:06:08] Maya: Security checklist: SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS, RBAC - can you send the security brief?
[00:06:12] Jordan: Yes we'll attach SOC2 and the security whitepaper. Also include a note on audit logs retention and SAML SSO integration notes.
[00:06:22] Lina: Network: VPC peering, private link options?
[00:06:25] Samira: We support VPC peering and private link, and can do customer-managed VPC endpoints. We'll put network diagrams in the doc.
[00:06:33] Ethan: How long is typical procurement and Dedicated onboarding?
[00:06:36] Jordan: For Hosted pilot - 1-2 weeks. Dedicated reserved with legal and procurement typically 6-10 weeks depending on contract. Private on-prem longer. But we can do a hosted pilot while procurement runs in parallel.
[00:06:50] Maya: OK good. Action items?
[00:06:52] Jordan: I'll send pricing spreadsheet + sample TCO, Samira will share benchmark runbook and harness links. We should schedule technical deep-dive with Lina and their infra team next week, 60 minutes.
[00:07:05] Maya: Works for us. Thanks.
